summary.headline: NBCC Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 38% YoY to INR 2,890 crore and standalone PAT rose 31% to INR 225 crore.
summary.overview: Standalone Q2 revenue from operations was INR 2,890 crore (consolidated INR 3,396 crore), up 38% YoY, with standalone EBITDA up 154% to INR 219 crore from INR 86 crore. Management attributed part of the margin expansion to about INR 100 crore of marketing fees in H1 (INR 88 crore in Q1) from Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs self-sustainable project sales, and said the revenue increase carries through a largely fixed cost base. Standalone order book stands at about INR 1,12,000 crore (consolidated INR 1,26,000 crore), and management reiterated FY27 standalone revenue guidance of INR 13,000-14,000 crore, with large order awards (Supertech, J&K, West Bengal, Bihar, 5 GPRA) expected through H2. Several order-inflow timelines were stated as near-term and remain unconverted as of the call.

financial_highlights.change: Down about INR 1,000 crore from March 2026 per analyst reconciliation; management cited no cancellations

financial_highlights.value: About 8% in Q2; about 9% in Q1

segments.name: Project management consultancy (PMC)
segments.commentary: About 40% of consolidated order book (53% of consolidated order book is PMC per management's split, which conflicts with the 40% stated for PMC; management said redevelopment 60% and PMC 40% of the order book, and 53-47% at consolidated level). Management said PMC projects typically take 3-4 years to complete.

segments.name: Redevelopment (self-sustainable / GPRA)
segments.commentary: Management said about 60% of the order book is redevelopment (47% at consolidated level by its own split). Balance workload: INR 9,200 crore on redevelopment packages; 7 GPRA sold Avenue Towers apartments of 8.8 lakh sq ft for INR 5,191 crore in e-auction. Management said 5,000 homes already handed over under 7 GPRA with another 9,000 units in progress.

segments.name: Amrapali
segments.commentary: Balance workload INR 8,000 crore in Phase II; 24 Phase I projects completed with handover in progress; one Phase II package reached 26 floors. Management said Phase II and 7 GPRA to be completed by end of next year.

segments.name: Real estate / land monetisation
segments.commentary: Sold two Jaipur land parcels for INR 250 crore and INR 180 crore (INR 433 crore total) against book value of about INR 195 crore, aggregate profit about INR 239 crore, with revenue and profit to be booked in Q4 per management. Land inventory of about 54 acres with book value INR 720 crore; IBBI valuation about INR 1,600 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone revenue guidance of INR 13,000-14,000 crore reaffirmed; H1 standalone revenue INR 4,713 crore, with management expecting Q2-Q4 to be stronger.
FY27 consolidated guidance: revenue INR 15,000-16,000 crore and PAT INR 1,100-1,200 crore (as stated on the call); management said it is maintaining guidance.
FY28 top line about INR 20,000-21,000 crore (consolidated) and PAT about INR 1,500 crore per management reply; standalone FY28 growth of 20-25% also referenced.
FY27 order inflow target INR 50,000-60,000 crore reaffirmed, including 5 GPRA (INR 30,000-35,000 crore); year-end order book guided at INR 1,80,000-2,00,000 crore after awards.
Running projects at consolidated level guided at about INR 40,000 crore by year-end; management said running projects currently about INR 33,000 crore.
capex_capacity: Supertech package tenders worth about INR 9,600 crore to be awarded in Q3 FY27, with turnover from Q4.
J&K: technical bids received on three tenders; price bids to open and about INR 2,000 crore work order expected in November 2026.
Ghitorni (4-4.5 lakh sq ft): final MoU and shareholder agreement pending, targeted by 31 December 2026; consultant tender under evaluation; construction from next year.
Sector 37-D project: contractor mobilised, piling started; sales launch targeted after 15 January 2027.

Dubai project: approvals and design obtained, RERA registration pending, groundbreaking targeted December 2026 or early in that month; sales phase 1 targeted end-December 2026 or January 2027; revenue recognised only on possession.
demand_pricing: West Bengal: nine MoUs signed with state departments; management estimated about INR 10,000 crore order potential; items include pink toilets (start Q4 FY27), riverfront, quarters, library and China Bazar redevelopment.
Bihar: about INR 2,000-3,000 crore received recently and four redevelopment projects of around INR 10,000 crore expected this year; MoU carries 1.25% marketing fee.
Africa Avenue (7 GPRA) auction: highest price INR 89,000 per sq ft against reserve price INR 37,160 per sq ft; NBCC earns 1% marketing fee on sales.
Scindia Marg and Vinayak Mandir Marg bulk sales targeted next quarter with sale value of about INR 8,000-10,000 crore (1% marketing fee).
Marketing fee guidance: about INR 100 crore in H2 FY27 and INR 200-250 crore in FY28 (management said 20-25% increase).

qa_highlights.question: Where are we against FY27 standalone revenue guidance of INR 13,000-14,000 crore, and what is the outlook for FY28-29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed INR 13,000-14,000 crore standalone for FY27, with H1 being slow and Q2-Q4 expected to deliver the balance; committed FY29 consolidated revenue of about INR 21,000 crore and 20-25% growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins and revenue rise this quarter, and were there one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA margin reached about 8% (Q1 about 9%) against a 5-6% prior range; about INR 100 crore of H1 marketing fee contributed, and the rest reflects revenue growth on a fixed cost base. Management said there were no one-offs and the income is recurring.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the order book not grown as guided, and what is the bottleneck in awards?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed delays to MAHAPREIT funding and approvals and the J&K tender timing; it now expects INR 15,000-16,000 crore of awards this year, with West Bengal and Bihar as potential upside.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the 5 GPRA project and the two large orders?
qa_highlights.answer: 5 GPRA (INR 30,000-35,000 crore) is awaiting cabinet approval, with award expected in Q3 or Q4 FY27; a border fencing order was also expected.

qa_highlights.question: What are the monetisation plans for land parcels and the associated tax and market value?
qa_highlights.answer: Land is carried as inventory, so profits are taxed at the normal rate per management; about 54 acres with book value INR 720 crore, IBBI valuation about INR 1,600 crore, with about INR 250 crore sold at market value; two more parcels in Meerut and Ghaziabad in auction.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected revenue conversion timeline for new orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PMC projects take 3-4 years and redevelopment 4-5 years for new awards, while awarded work converts within 18-24 months, with execution at 24-30 months currently.

risks_watch: Order inflow conversion: management guided INR 50,000-60,000 crore of FY27 inflows, but H1 awards were only INR 3,200 crore consolidated; large awards (5 GPRA, Supertech, J&K, West Bengal) remain pending and timing has repeatedly slipped.

Consolidated order book fell about INR 1,000 crore from March 2026 to September 2026 (INR 1,27,000 crore to INR 1,26,000 crore) with new awards of about INR 5,000 crore in H1, indicating conversion above awards.
Delhi air-quality (AQI) construction stoppages can halt work at Delhi projects, per management.

Margin sustainability: Q2 EBITDA margin includes about INR 100 crore of one-time-like marketing fee income in H1; land monetisation (INR 433 crore revenue, INR 200 crore profit) is expected to book in Q4 FY27.

Policy and approval dependence: MAHAPREIT and Naveen Nagpur delayed by funding and approvals; Rajasthan Mandapam tender (INR 4,000 crore, possibly INR 5,500 crore) deferred by election code; Mumbai Port Trust (INR 10,000 crore) pending a shift to redevelopment model.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on order pipeline and FY27-29 targets, repeatedly reaffirming guidance and naming specific award timelines; more cautious and vague when pressed on order-inflow delays, the MAHAPREIT funding status and the timing of GPRA/Supertech awards, where answers were largely qualitative.

adds.what: Dubai project groundbreaking (real estate development, not owned productive capacity)

growth.why: FY27 standalone revenue guidance of INR 13,000-14,000 cr (about 13% midpoint growth implied vs H1 standalone INR 4,713 cr, +26%) reaffirmed, backed by a standalone order book of about INR 1,12,000 cr and a stated FY27 order inflow target of INR 50,000-60,000 cr, but H1 awards were only about INR 3,200 cr so the H2 ramp depends on unconverted tenders (Supertech, J&K, 5 GPRA) and no owned capacity i

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 standalone EBITDA margin about 8% (Q1 about 9%) vs prior 5-6% guide, but about INR 100 crore of H1 marketing fee lifts it and management guides marketing fee of about INR 100 crore in H2 FY27, so underlying margin gain is unproven.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: NBCC is a consultancy/contractor with no owned productive capacity; growth comes from order execution on a largely fixed cost base, and the Dubai and Ghitorni items are real-estate development rather than capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Standalone H1 revenue INR 4,713 crore (+26% YoY) and FY27 guidance INR 13,000-14,000 crore implies H2 of about INR 8,300-9,300 crore; standalone order book INR 1,12,000 crore and running projects about INR 33,000 crore support execution, though FY28 growth of 20-25% is guided.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the brief records no utilisation level and no owned-capacity plan.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reaffirmed FY27 guidance but H1 awards were only INR 3,200 crore against INR 50,000-60,000 crore inflow target, and the order book fell about INR 1,000 crore, so an upgrade is not supported.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 awards of INR 3,200 crore against a INR 50,000-60,000 crore target, and key awards (5 GPRA INR 30,000-35,000 crore, Supertech about INR 9,600 crore, J&K about INR 2,000 crore) have repeatedly slipped; the consolidated order book fell about INR 1,000 crore since March 2026.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Sector 37-D sales launch is targeted after 15 January 2027 and Dubai phase 1 sales end-December 2026 or January 2027, with pink toilets starting Q4 FY27 in West Bengal.

rows.label: Large order awards (5 GPRA, Supertech, J&K, West Bengal, Bihar)
rows.why: Management guides INR 15,000-16,000 crore of awards this year vs H1 consolidated awards of INR 3,200 crore; Supertech INR 9,600 crore targeted Q3 FY27, J&K about INR 2,000 crore expected November 2026, 5 GPRA awaiting cabinet approval, but timelines have slipped repeatedly.

rows.label: Jaipur land monetisation booked in Q4
rows.why: Two Jaipur parcels sold for INR 433 crore against book value about INR 195 crore, aggregate profit about INR 239 crore, with revenue and profit to be booked in Q4 per management.

rows.label: Dubai project and Ghitorni launch
rows.why: Dubai groundbreaking targeted December 2026 with sales phase 1 end-December 2026 or January 2027 but RERA registration pending; Ghitorni (4-4.5 lakh sq ft) MoU targeted by 31 December 2026, construction from next year.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27-29 targets, reaffirming guidance and naming award timelines, but was vague when pressed on order-inflow delays, MAHAPREIT funding and GPRA/Supertech timing; analysts focused on the gap between H1 awards and the INR 50,000-60,000 crore target.
